title: Magnetic Forces and Induction
seo_title: Physics 12: Magnetic Forces and Induction Worksheets (BC Curriculum)

standard_text: Electromagnetism: magnetic fields, the force on moving charges and on current-carrying wires, electromagnetic induction, Faraday's and Lenz's laws, motors, generators and transformers. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 12)
meta_desc: Free Physics 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): magnetic force, induction, motors and generators. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A changing magnetic flux induces a voltage.
key_sub: F = BIL for a wire; F = qvB for a charge.
body_html:
How to think about it

A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field feels a force F = BIL (when perpendicular); a moving charge feels F = qvB. The direction is given by a hand rule. Electric motors use this force to turn a coil.

Faraday's law: a changing magnetic flux through a coil induces a voltage. Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change that caused it. Generators turn a coil in a field to make AC; transformers change voltage: Vs ÷ Vp = Ns ÷ Np.

Example

A 0.50 m wire carries 4.0 A at right angles to a 0.20 T field. What is the force?

F = BIL

Answer: 0.40 N

Example

A transformer has 100 primary and 500 secondary turns. 120 V in gives how much out?

Vs = Vp × Ns ÷ Np

Answer: 600 V

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a steady magnetic field induces a current.
  • Thinking transformers work with DC.
  • Getting the direction from the wrong hand rule.

faq.q: Why does a magnet fall slowly through a copper pipe?
faq.a: Induced currents in the pipe make a field that opposes the motion (Lenz's law).

faq.q: Why is electricity sent at high voltage?
faq.a: Higher voltage means lower current and less energy lost as heat.
